subject: Electrical Engineering
title: First-Order Systems: Exponential Response
description: A quick win: understand First-Order Systems: Exponential Response.

hook.text: Fill a cup with hot water and watch it cool. Temperature drops in a smooth exponential curve.

buildup.text: A first-order system has one pole. Its step response is a rising exponential toward the new setpoint.

discovery.text: The time constant τ sets the speed: after one τ, the output reaches 63% of the final value.

twist.text: After five time constants, the output is within 1% of the final value — practically settled.

climax.text: RC circuits, thermal systems, and first-order chemical reactions all follow this pattern.

punchline.text: One pole, one time constant — the simplest dynamic model.

quiz.question: After one time constant τ, what percentage of the final value has a first-order system reached?
